en: The graph rule judges what the compiler built rather than what a record asserts, and it has one judge: every finding is one the compiler emits while it extracts, and <t1/>, <t2/> and <t3/> only classify it. Which break fails is decided by where the relationship was stated. One Majordomus derives from a structured field — an issue's <t4/> and <t5/>, a claim's <t6/>, <t7/> and <t8/>, a rule's dependency — is owned, and a broken one fails the command (exit 10), warns under <t9/>, where the rule is advisory, and is drift under <t10/>. A link an author wrote in prose may point outside the repository on purpose, so a target it names that resolves to nothing is reported and never fails; <t11/> and <t12/> summarise those in one line. A tracked source the working tree no longer holds is reported as <t13/> — a deletion in progress — and is drift under <t14/>. No generated graph is stored (I0810 was cancelled because none exists), so there is no index to go stale and no stored hash to mismatch; the command says so on every run, and <t15/> answers whether the graph can be built here by compiling it into a temporary file it removes. Nothing is rebuilt or repaired.
cs: Pravidlo grafu posuzuje to, co kompilátor sestavil, ne to, co záznam tvrdí, a má jednoho soudce: každé zjištění je takové, které kompilátor vydá při extrakci, a <t1/>, <t2/> a <t3/> ho jen klasifikují. Odkaz, který autor napsal v próze, může záměrně mířit mimo repozitář, takže cíl, který pojmenovává a který se na nic nerozřeší, se hlásí a nikdy neselže; <t11/> a <t12/> je shrnují na jednom řádku. en: It is not a second application. It has no datastore, no status vocabulary and no route list of its own beyond the screens its dispatcher answers. It does not replace the Cockpit, which stays the technical layer (ADR 0135), and it writes nothing: an action on it is a capability with its own route.
